field.label: Enable
field.help: Starts the appaliasd DNS relay and the synchronization of the APP_* aliases.

field.label: Listen addresses
field.help: Addresses the relay listens on, comma separated. Default 127.0.0.1: only the local resolver (Unbound or Dnsmasq) queries it. Add a LAN address (and set the port to 53) to serve LAN clients directly, for example when no resolver runs on the firewall: then point the DHCP DNS of your clients to the firewall. Clients outside the allowed networks are ignored.

field.label: Listen port
field.help: UDP and TCP port of the relay (default 53535).

field.label: Response cache
field.help: Answers are cached according to their TTL (bounded by minimum TTL + TTL margin) and served without asking the upstream; the aliases are still refreshed. Recommended when LAN clients query the relay directly.

field.label: Allowed client networks
field.help: Only queries from these networks are answered. Empty: loopback and private networks (RFC 1918, ULA, link-local). Queries from other addresses are dropped without answer.

field.label: Rate limit per client (queries/s)
field.help: Queries per second accepted from one client address (burst: twice this value). 0 = unlimited. Loopback is never limited.

field.label: pf backend
field.help: How addresses are written to the pf tables. Automatic: direct ioctl on /dev/pf (no process per answer), with fallback to the pfctl command if the ioctl fails at startup. The active backend is shown in the status above.

field.label: ASN sources
field.help: The prefixes announced in BGP by the ASNs of an application (RIPEstat, https://stat.ripe.net) are added to its alias. Refreshed once a day and after Apply; RIPE NCC sees the address of the firewall. Uncheck to never contact RIPEstat.

field.label: Upstream resolver
field.help: IP address of the resolver the relay forwards every query to, unchanged. Required when the service is enabled.

field.label: Upstream protocol
field.help: Plain DNS, or DNS over TLS (RFC 7858) to encrypt the queries of the application domains up to the upstream. With DNS over TLS the certificate and its name are always checked, and the relay never falls back to plain DNS: on failure it tries the next fallback upstream, then answers SERVFAIL. Example (Quad9): resolver 9.9.9.9, port 853, TLS name dns.quad9.net.

field.label: Upstream port
field.help: 53 for plain DNS, 853 for DNS over TLS (set automatically when you change the protocol, unless the port is custom). Port 53 with DNS over TLS and port 853 with plain DNS are refused.

field.label: Upstream TLS name
field.help: DNS over TLS only, required: name checked in the certificate of the upstream and sent as SNI, for example dns.quad9.net for 9.9.9.9. Also used by the fallback upstreams without their own #name.

field.label: Fallback upstreams
field.help: Tried in order when the main upstream does not answer, with the same protocol. Format: ip, ip:port, [ipv6] or [ipv6]:port, optionally followed by #tls-name (DNS over TLS). Default port: 53 (plain DNS) or 853 (DNS over TLS); default TLS name: the one of the main upstream. Example: 149.112.112.112#dns.quad9.net.

field.label: Forward application domains from Unbound
field.help: Unbound sends only the domains of the enabled applications to the relay, one forward zone per domain (file /usr/local/etc/unbound.opnsense.d/appalias.conf). Other queries keep their usual path (DNS over TLS, Query Forwarding). Names already configured in Unbound (Query Forwarding, DNS over TLS, domain overrides) and local names are skipped. Applying restarts Unbound when the list of forwarded domains changes. Each zone uses forward-first: while the relay is down, Unbound falls back to direct recursion to the authoritative servers for these domains (plain DNS on UDP/TCP port 53), bypassing DNS over TLS and the "." Query Forwarding; their addresses are not added to the aliases. If outgoing port 53 is blocked, these domains fail (SERVFAIL) until the relay is back. After adding a Query Forwarding entry for a domain also used by AppAlias, press Apply in AppAlias. Leave unchecked to set up the forwarding by hand.

field.label: Follow CNAMEs
field.help: Names of the CNAME chain of an answer are matched too.

field.label: Minimum TTL (s)
field.help: An address stays at least this long in the table, even if the DNS TTL is shorter.

field.label: TTL margin (s)
field.help: Time added to the expiry of each address (covers client caches). Expiry = now + max(TTL, minimum TTL) + margin.

field.label: Max. entries per application
field.help: Beyond this, no address is added any more and a message is logged.

field.label: Excluded networks
field.help: Resolved addresses in these networks are never added (private, local addresses, etc.).

field.label: Extra shared platforms
field.help: Names added to the built-in list of shared platforms (CDN, cloud, hosting). A "domain:" rule equal to one of them, or a parent of one, is refused.

field.label: Proactive resolution
field.help: The relay resolves by itself, at regular intervals, the "domain:" and "full:" names of the enabled applications that have the option checked, to fill the aliases before any client asks. It works in addition to the DNS relay, not instead of it: dynamic names, "regexp:" and "keyword:" rules and shared platforms (CDN, cloud) are not covered. It generates outgoing DNS traffic towards the upstream resolver.

field.label: Deep discovery
field.help: In addition to the domain itself and the proactive prefixes, the relay probes a built-in dictionary of about 90 common service labels (api, chat, cdn, storage, voip...) in front of each domain: rule, so the real endpoints of an application enter the alias before any client asks. Domains that answer any name (DNS wildcard) are detected and skipped, as are domains that do not exist (NXDOMAIN). This option only controls the dictionary: built-in hints for popular applications and names already seen by the relay are always probed while Proactive resolution is enabled. Adds DNS traffic towards the upstream after each change, then NXDOMAIN names back off.

field.label: Seed from Unbound cache
field.help: At startup, after Apply and every hour, the names already resolved by Unbound (unbound-control dump_cache) that match an application are added to its alias at once, with their addresses. Requires Unbound on the firewall.

field.label: Proactive minimum interval (s)
field.help: Shortest delay between two resolutions of a name (60 to 86400). Must not exceed the maximum interval.

field.label: Proactive maximum interval (s)
field.help: Longest delay between two resolutions of a name (300 to 86400). Must stay below minimum TTL + TTL margin, otherwise addresses would expire between two passes.

field.label: Proactive prefixes
field.help: Labels tried in front of each "domain:" rule, for example www gives www.example.com (8 at most; letters, digits or "-", no dot). The domain itself is always resolved.

field.label: Download catalog updates
field.help: On by default: once a day (and after the plugin is installed or upgraded), the firewall downloads the latest v2fly/domain-list-community from GitHub (api.github.com, codeload.github.com), so GitHub sees the address of the firewall. "Update catalog now" in the Catalog tab does it at once. A download only refreshes the catalog: nothing is applied to your applications, new rules are shown as catalog updates to review. Uncheck to stay offline with the snapshot embedded in the package.

field.label: Catalog update schedule
field.help: Hourly (default): the online list is checked every hour, at a minute derived from the host name (cron job, only while the download option is checked). Each check is a single API call; the archive is downloaded only if the list has changed, and applications that follow the catalog are then updated automatically. Daily: the same check once a day. Manual: only with "Update catalog now".

field.label: Alias prefix
field.help: Alias name = prefix + application name (31 characters at most).
